task.name: Whether an agent acted on injected prior-run knowledge is never recorded, so the loop can be seen delivering and seen being ignored but never seen landing
task.story_text:
The knowledge loop now records what was injected into a run and how much of the prompt it
consumed, and it records the negative case — a reviewer raising a finding that repeats a
claim the developer had already been given. Nothing records the positive case. Whether an
agent read an injected claim, acted on it, and changed what it did as a result is not
observed anywhere, so the one question the loop exists to answer — is the knowledge
reaching the point of use — cannot be asked of the artifacts.

The instrument that would answer it is not an opinion. Asking an agent whether the context
was useful produces agreement at a rate that carries no information, and a satisfaction
number that cannot fail is worse than no number, because it will be believed. The
instrument is a receipt: at the end of each phase that received injected knowledge, the
agent names each claim it was given, states what it did with it, and for any claim it says
it used, points at the observable consequence — the plan section, the change, the test, or
the verification it prompted. The system then checks that the named claim was in fact
injected into that phase and that the pointed-at consequence exists, and reports a corroborated
use claim separately from an uncorroborated one. Corroboration establishes that the cited
consequence exists; it does not establish that the injected knowledge caused it, and no
readout may present it as though it did.

This answers the practical question directly, from the runs already happening, with no
control arm and nothing withheld. It does not establish counterfactual cost, and it is not
meant to; it establishes whether the loop lands, which is the decision that determines
whether the randomized cost experiment is worth building at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- A phase that received injected prior-run knowledge produces a debrief listing every claim
  it was given, each with a disposition. A phase that received nothing produces no debrief
  and is reported as having had nothing to debrief; a phase that received claims and
  returned no debrief is reported as undebriefed. Neither absence is ever reported as
  "unused".

- Every debrief entry is matched against the recorded exposure for that phase. An entry
  naming a claim that was not injected into that phase is recorded as an unmatched citation
  and excluded from every count of use. A claim that was injected and does not appear in the
  debrief is recorded as unaddressed, distinct from any disposition the agent could have
  chosen.

- Any disposition asserting that a claim influenced the work carries a pointer to an
  observable consequence in that run's artifacts, and the system resolves the pointer. A
  resolvable pointer whose target contains the described consequence yields a corroborated
  use claim; an unresolvable or absent pointer yields an uncorroborated use claim. The two
  are reported as separate populations, no readout sums them, and neither is named or
  presented as verified, confirmed, or effective use.

- The debrief schema has no field for usefulness, satisfaction, confidence, or a
  counterfactual. A disposition is a category the agent selects from a closed set; free
  text is limited to describing what was done, and it contributes to no count.

- The closed set of dispositions distinguishes at least: the claim changed a decision, the
  claim prompted a verification, the claim confirmed an approach already taken, the claim
  was irrelevant to the task, the claim was already known, and the claim was judged stale
  or wrong. A disposition outside the set is recorded as unrecognised and excluded, never
  mapped onto a nearby one.

- The debrief and its verification are recorded per run and per phase in the audit
  substrate and surfaced by the knowledge report as counts of corroborated use claims,
  uncorroborated use claims, each non-use disposition, unmatched citations, unaddressed
  claims, and undebriefed phases. The report presents these as a distribution, states that
  no effectiveness or return-on-investment conclusion follows, and draws none.

- The instrument is audit-only. Nothing in routing, selection, readiness, or landing reads
  the debrief. Its output changes what an operator can see and nothing the system decides.

## Example

A dev phase received three injected claims. Its debrief:

```
- claim: 7f3a…   disposition: changed_decision
  did: added the projection rebuild path to the plan before implementing
  evidence: plan §3; commit touching the rebuild entry point
- claim: c91e…   disposition: already_known
  did: matched the approach I had already taken
- claim: b204…   disposition: stale_or_wrong
  did: the behaviour it describes was replaced in the current release
```

The system confirms all three claims were injected into this dev phase. For the first, it
resolves both pointers, finds the described consequence in each, and records a
**corroborated use claim**. The second and third are non-use
dispositions and are counted as such.

A different run's debrief cites a fourth claim that was never injected into that phase; it
is recorded as an **unmatched citation** and appears in no use count. A third run received two claims
and returned a debrief naming only one; the other is recorded as **unaddressed**.

The knowledge report then reads, over a window of runs:

```
phases with injected knowledge   41
  debriefed                      38     undebriefed  3
claims injected                 112
  corroborated use claims        19
  uncorroborated use claims       7
  confirmed existing approach    24
  already known                  31
  irrelevant                     18
  stale or wrong                  6
  unaddressed                     5
  unmatched citations             2
```

Beneath the table the report reads: *Corroborated uptake claims: 19 of 112 exposed claims.
No effectiveness or ROI conclusion follows.* Nineteen of 112 is the number the operator was
missing; what it means is the operator's judgement, and the report makes none.

claims.claim: Review-only handling for batched non-leader stories must use the same per-story diff-grounding rules as the main review flow, or sibling findings can still fail the wrong story.

Batch-member grounding has to be computed from the member story's own diff rather than a leader or shared-worktree combined diff, otherwise sibling stories in the same batch can be treated as relevant evidence.

A finding's grounding status needs to be recomputed each review cycle from current story evidence, because a previously ungrounded P1 can later become grounded and should then participate in blocking decisions.
Non-blocking dispositions for ungrounded findings must be honored consistently by escalation and topology analysis, not just by the immediate review verdict path.

handoff.summary: Added an audit-only prior-run knowledge receipt instrument. A new pure verifier module (knowledge_receipts.py) defines the closed six-way disposition taxonomy, extracts claim exposure per phase from context_manifests[*].prior_run_context, matches debrief entries against it, resolves evidence pointers deterministically against the run's own recorded artifacts (changed files, plan sections/steps, commits, tests), and collapses to one counted disposition per (phase, claim_ref) with a conservative precedence so multi-reviewer disagreement never resolves into a use count. Claim references are now rendered into the prior-run claim lines agents actually read, produced by the same claim_reference function the exposure manifest stores (moved to prior_run_selector, re-exported from prior_run_manifest). A new task/debrief_prompts.py renders the debrief instruction into PLAN, DEV, and REVIEW prompts only when the assembled pack carried claims; review_json_schema gains knowledge_debrief as a required-nullable property so strict-mode API reviewers can carry it without relaxing verdict fields. The coordinator captures raw submissions into state.knowledge_debriefs at three seams (dev handoff, plan YAML, every reviewer including the quorum-collapse path) without branching on content, and generate_audit_log writes the verified knowledge_receipts block onto the record. Record schema bumped 45 to 46 with _migrate_v45_to_v46 lifting pre-instrument records to uncomparable_pre_capture and a new v46 fixture. knowledge_receipts_report.py aggregates bounded records into a distribution surfaced by forge knowledge-report as its own section in terminal/JSON/YAML.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 review fix. The P1 was that evidence-pointer resolution accepted category *existence* as corroboration: commit, test, and unqualified-plan pointers resolved whenever the run had recorded any artifact of that kind, so 'a commit touching the rebuild entry point' was counted as a corroborated use claim against a README-only commit. The flaw was in three of the four pointer kinds rather than just the reported commit line, so all three were fixed at the root via a new _resolve_category_pointer: a category pointer now resolves only when its own distinguishing words (category nouns and connectives removed via _POINTER_NOISE_TOKENS) match one specific recorded candidate's text, and a bare 'a commit'/'the test'/'the plan' identifies nothing and never corroborates. Path and section pointers already named a specific target and are unchanged. Fixing this exposed a tokenization defect — [a-z0-9_]+ made tests/test_rebuild.py yield 'test_rebuild' and never 'rebuild' — so a shared _tokenize now also splits underscored names while keeping the unsplit form, still matching whole tokens and never substrings. Added the negative coverage the review named as missing (broad commit/test/unqualified-plan pointers staying uncorroborated when the recorded artifact lacks the consequence), plus bare-category and tokenization cases, and replaced the one parametrized case that had encoded the buggy behaviour. Prompt and docs now state that a pointer must identify one artifact, since an unresolvable pointer is an acceptable outcome and a vague one resolving against the wrong artifact is not.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A phase that received injected prior-run knowledge produces a debrief listing every claim it was given, each with a disposition. A phase that received nothing produces no debrief and is reported as having had nothing to debrief; a phase that received claims and returned no debrief is reported as undebriefed. Neither absence is ever reported as "unused".

Every debrief entry is matched against the recorded exposure for that phase. An entry naming a claim that was not injected into that phase is recorded as an unmatched citation and excluded from every count of use. A claim that was injected and does not appear in the debrief is recorded as unaddressed, distinct from any disposition the agent could have chosen.

Any disposition asserting that a claim influenced the work carries a pointer to an observable consequence in that run's artifacts, and the system resolves the pointer. A resolvable pointer whose target contains the described consequence yields a corroborated use claim; an unresolvable or absent pointer yields an uncorroborated use claim. The two are reported as separate populations, no readout sums them, and neither is named or presented as verified, confirmed, or effective use.

The debrief schema has no field for usefulness, satisfaction, confidence, or a counterfactual. A disposition is a category the agent selects from a closed set; free text is limited to describing what was done, and it contributes to no count.

The closed set of dispositions distinguishes at least: the claim changed a decision, the claim prompted a verification, the claim confirmed an approach already taken, the claim was irrelevant to the task, the claim was already known, and the claim was judged stale or wrong. A disposition outside the set is recorded as unrecognised and excluded, never mapped onto a nearby one.

The debrief and its verification are recorded per run and per phase in the audit substrate and surfaced by the knowledge report as counts of corroborated use claims, uncorroborated use claims, each non-use disposition, unmatched citations, unaddressed claims, and undebriefed phases. The report presents these as a distribution, states that no effectiveness or return-on-investment conclusion follows, and draws none.
